DefiLlama offers two ways to use our data with AI: | Resource | For | Description | |---|---|---| | llms.txt | AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, etc.) | Paste this link into your AI assistant for LLM-optimized docs | | MCP Server | AI agents | Connect your agent directly to DefiLlama data — 23 tools, uses API credits | **Quick start (MCP)** — paste this into your AI agent: ``` Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DefiLlama/defillama-skills/refs/heads/master/defillama-setup/SKILL.md and follow the instructions to connect to DefiLlama MCP ``` --- Docs for DefiLlama's Pro API ## SDK **JavaScript** — `npm install @defillama/api` — [GitHub](https://github.com/DefiLlama/api-sdk) **Python** — `pip install defillama-sdk` — [GitHub](https://github.com/DefiLlama/python-sdk) Quick start (JavaScript): ```ts import { DefiLlama } from '@defillama/api' const proClient = new DefiLlama({ apiKey: 'your-api-key' }) const protocols = await proClient.tvl.getProtocols() ``` Quick start (Python): ```py from defillama_sdk import DefiLlama pro_client = DefiLlama({"api_key": "your-api-key"}) protocols = pro_client.tvl.getProtocols() ```

tags.name: yields
tags.description:
Data from our yields/APY dashboard

> [!WARNING]
> **The original yield endpoints stop working on November 13, 2026.** If you call any endpoint on the left of an arrow below, migrate before then. From that date the yield API requires the [API plan](https://defillama.com/subscription). The yields dashboards at [defillama.com/yields](https://defillama.com/yields) stay free for everyone.

### How to migrate

**Option 1, minimal: swap the URL.** The `/yields/v1/` routes keep today's response format, so the URL is the only thing you change. They exist for compatibility only: all new features land on v2.

- `/pools`, `/yields/pools`, `/yields/poolsOld` → `/yields/v1/pools`
- `/chart/{pool}`, `/yields/chart/{pool}` → `/yields/v1/chart/{pool}`
- `/yields/poolsBorrow` → `/yields/v1/poolsBorrow`
- `/yields/chartLendBorrow/{pool}` → `/yields/v1/chartLendBorrow/{pool}`
- `/yields/lsdRates` → `/api/lstRates`

**Option 2, recommended: move to v2.** New response format, so this takes some integration work, but you get all the new features (Verified APY etc, see below).

- `/pools`, `/yields/pools`, `/yields/poolsOld` → `/yields/v2/earn`
- `/chart/{pool}`, `/yields/chart/{pool}` → `/yields/v2/earn/{id}/history`
- `/yields/poolsBorrow` → `/yields/v2/borrow/markets`
- `/yields/chartLendBorrow/{pool}` → `/yields/v2/borrow/markets/{id}/history` (borrow side) and `/yields/v2/earn/{id}/history` (lend side)
- `/yields/lsdRates` → `/api/lstRates` (no v2 version)

Good to know:

- Pool IDs are unchanged, so nothing needs re-mapping.
- `/yields/v1/pools` serves the `/poolsOld` format, which contains all the `/pools` fields, so parsers for either endpoint keep working.
- Some legacy statistics fields (e.g. `predictions`) are always null on the `/yields/v1/` routes.

### What is new in v2

- **Verified APY** at `/yields/v2/earn/verified`: every day we simulate real holder withdrawals on-chain and record what they actually receive, not what protocols report
- 10-minute refreshes instead of hourly
- A borrow router at `/yields/v2/borrow/routes`: the best rate across thousands of pools in one call
- APYs split into base, reward and intrinsic components, with 7- and 30-day averages built in

Returns protocol metadata, methodology details, and aggregated financial statement data (yearly, quarterly, monthly). Each period contains line items such as Gross Protocol Revenue, Cost Of Revenue, Gross Profit, Token Holder Net Income, Incentives, and Earnings, with values and optional label breakdowns.

Gross Protocol Revenue.Borrow Interest GHO: All interest paid by borrowers from GHO only.

Cost Of Revenue.Borrow Interest: Amount of interest distributed to lenders from all markets (excluding GHO).

Gross Profit.Borrow Interest: A portion of interest paid by borrowers from all markets (excluding GHO).
Gross Profit.Borrow Interest GHO: All 100% interest paid by GHO borrowers.
Gross Profit.Liquidation Fees: A portion of fees from liquidation penalty and bonuses.

Get current prices of tokens by contract address
get.description:
The goal of this API is to price as many tokens as possible, including exotic ones that never get traded, which makes them impossible to price by looking at markets.

The base of our data are prices pulled from coingecko, which is then extended through multiple means:
- We price all bridged tokens by using the price of the token in it's original chain, so we fetch all bridged versions of USDC on arbitrum, fantom, avax... and price all them using the price for the token on Ethereum, which we know. Right now we support 10 different bridging protocols.
- We have multiple adapters to price specialized sets of tokens by running custom code:
  - We price yearn's yToken LPs by checking how much underlying token can be withdrawn for each LP
  - Aave, compound and euler LP tokens are also priced based on their relationship against underlying tokens
  - Uniswap, curve, balancer and stargate LPs are priced using the underlying tokens in each pair
  - GMX's GLP token is priced based on the value of tokens given on withdrawal (which includes calculations based on trader's PnL)
  
  - Synthetix tokens are priced using forex prices of the coin they are pegged to
- For tokens that we haven't been able to price in any other way, we find the pool with most liquidity for each on uniswap, curve and serum and then use the prices provided on those exchanges.
  
  Unlike all the other tokens, we can't confirm that these prices are correct, so we only ingest the ones that have sufficient liquidity and, even in that case, we attach a `confidence` value to them that is related to the depth of liquidity and which represents our confidence in the quality of each price. API consumers can choose to filter out prices with low confidence values.
  
 Our API server is fully open source and we are constantly adding more pricing adapters, extending the amount of tokens we support.
  
Tokens are queried using {chain}:{address}, where chain is an identifier such as ethereum, bsc, polygon, avax... You can also get tokens by coingecko id by setting `coingecko` as the chain, eg: coingecko:ethereum, coingecko:bitcoin. Examples:
  - ethereum:0xdF574c24545E5FfEcb9a659c229253D4111d87e1
  - bsc:0x762539b45a1dcce3d36d080f74d1aed37844b878
  - coingecko:ethereum
  - arbitrum:0x4277f8f2c384827b5273592ff7cebd9f2c1ac258

get.summary: Get earnings calendar
get.description:
Returns earnings report dates built from SEC EDGAR filings: past reports, plus the next four expected dates projected from each company's own filing history. Covers US-listed companies.

The same path serves two shapes:

- **With `ticker`**: that company's full history plus its upcoming estimates.
- **Without `ticker`**: the market-wide calendar over a rolling window from about 1 month back to about 13 months ahead. Use the `ticker` form for older history.

Rows are sorted by `report_date`, oldest first, so `limit` keeps the earliest matches. `?ticker=AAPL&status=estimated&limit=1` is Apple's next report.

Every row says what kind of date it is in `date_status`. A future date is `estimated`, with a `max_drift_days` range, and is not a confirmed schedule.

Company names are not included. Join on `ticker` against `GET /equities/v1/companies-list`.

parameters.name: ticker
parameters.description: Stock ticker symbol (case-insensitive). When set, returns that company's full calendar.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Earliest `report_date` to include, as `YYYY-MM-DD` (inclusive).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Latest `report_date` to include, as `YYYY-MM-DD` (inclusive).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only return rows with this `date_status` (case-insensitive). `confirmed` is accepted but nothing produces it yet, so it returns an empty list.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return, taken from the earliest `report_date`. Positive integer; values above 20000 are capped at 20000.

X-Total-Matches.description: Rows matching the filters before `limit` was applied.

cik.description: SEC CIK of the registrant that filed the row. Differs from the company's current CIK for rows inherited from a predecessor after a reorganisation.

event_key.description: `<fiscal_year>-<fiscal_period>`, the row's identity. When the report arrives, its row replaces the estimate with the same key.

date_status.description: `reported`: an earnings release (8-K Item 2.02) was filed. `inferred`: no release that quarter, so the date comes from the 10-Q or 10-K (filing-backed, but weaker). `estimated`: projected from the company's past cadence. `confirmed`: announced by the company; not produced yet.

report_date.description: US Eastern date of the report, from the SEC acceptance timestamp rather than EDGAR's filing date.

report_time.description: `bmo`: before 09:30 ET. `dmt`: during market hours. `amc`: after 16:00 ET. `unknown`: no timestamp, as on estimates. Taken from the SEC acceptance time, not the newswire.

accepted_at.description: Raw SEC acceptance timestamp, in UTC. Empty on estimates.

fiscal_year.description: Fiscal year the quarter belongs to, named for the calendar year it ends in.

period_end.description: Last day of the fiscal period the report covers. Empty for a release whose 10-Q has not been filed yet, and for estimates projected from one.

source.description: `8k_item_202`: an earnings release. `periodic_filing`: a 10-Q or 10-K, used when there was no release. `cadence_model`: an estimate.

source_form.description: SEC form the date comes from, such as `8-K`, `10-Q` or `10-K`. Empty on estimates.

accession_number.description: SEC accession number of that filing. Empty on estimates.

max_drift_days.description: On estimates, how many days either side of `report_date` the real date may land. 96% of real dates fell inside this range when tested against past reports. Wider for small caps and short histories. `null` on filing-backed rows.

first_published_at.description: When this `event_key` was first published (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.sss`).

revision_count.description: How many times the filing-backed date has moved since it was first published.

previous_report_date.description: The `report_date` before the most recent move. Empty if it never moved.

inserted_at.description: When this row was last written (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.sss`).

400.description: `limit` is not a positive integer (`{"error": "Invalid limit"}`)

404.description: `ticker` is not a tracked company (`{"error": "Earnings calendar not found"}`)

500.description: Invalid or missing API key (`{"error": "API Key is wrong"}`), or an internal server error

get.summary: Get valuation history for a pre-IPO company
get.description: Returns one aggregated valuation point per calendar month, oldest first. Within a month every source's marks are averaged and then the source averages are averaged, so a source that reports daily does not outvote one that reports monthly. Points are rounded to the nearest 100 and dated `YYYY-MM-01`; months with no data are skipped, and the current month is month-to-date.

get.summary: Get tradeable markets for a pre-IPO company
get.description: Returns where the company can actually be traded right now: perpetual futures venues and tokenised-share issuers. A pre-IPO perp settles in stablecoins against the venue's reference price, so no shares change hands and the same company can trade at a slightly different price on every venue. This is a live snapshot refreshed hourly and no history is kept. Every company in the registry gets a response: one with no listings returns empty `perps` and `tokenIssuers` arrays rather than a miss.

parameters.description: Company id from `GET /pre-ipo/v1/companies-list` (case-insensitive). The display `name` is not accepted.

backing.description: What the token is a claim on, ordered from the most direct claim on the underlying shares to the least. `Direct shares` and `Trust-held SPV` are asset-backed and bankruptcy-remote, `SPV interest` is asset-backed but held one layer removed through a vehicle, and `Unsecured note` and `Synthetic` are not asset-backed at all.

marketCap.description: Market cap of the token, in USD. Only populated for issuers that publish one.

estimatedValuation.description: Company valuation implied by the token price, in USD.
